display.purpose: The 'raygent dashboard' wordmark only. Rajdhani, self-hosted.

label.purpose: Column headers, stat unit labels, meta rows -- uppercase, tracked.

data.purpose: Every numeric readout -- tabular monospace so figures line up across rows.

shadows.name: console-lift
shadows.purpose: The system's only shadow -- applied once, to the console panel.

shadows.name: revenue-glow
shadows.purpose: Cyan glow on the revenue figure and the ring mark's drop-shadow -- the accent's only 'lit' treatment.

motion.name: ring-pulse
motion.purpose: The page's one authored ambient motion, on the ring mark only. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: row-hover
motion.purpose: The only interactive state transition; not an ambient effect.

components.name: Console Panel
components.description: The whole page's one structural component -- a bordered, gradient-filled plate holding a header row and N product rows.
components.css: .ds-console { background: linear-gradient(165deg, #161d28 0%, #10151d 100%); border: 1px solid #2a3542; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.03) inset, 0 14px 30px -18px rgba(0,0,0,0.65); overflow: hidden; } .ds-console-head { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 0.9fr 1.3fr 1fr; gap: 18px; padding: 14px 20px; color: #8b98a8; font-family: Rajdhani, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; border-bottom: 1px solid #2a3542; }

components.name: Product Row
components.description: One product's data: name/meta, revenue, a 3-up stat trio, and a 14-day activity readout. No border/shadow/radius of its own -- hairline divider only.

components.css: .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 0.9fr 1.3fr 1fr; gap: 18px; align-items: center; padding: 14px 20px; border-top: 1px solid #202932; transition: background 140ms ease; } .ds-row:hover { background: rgba(79,211,232,0.04); } .ds-row-id h2 { font-family: Rajdhani, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #e7edf5; } .ds-meta { color: #8b98a8; font-size: 10.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-revenue-value { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #4fd3e8; text-shadow: 0 0 16px rgba(79,211,232,0.4); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-revenue-label { color: #8b98a8; font-size: 10px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; }

components.name: Ring Mark
components.description: The brand motif: a small SVG with a static outer ring, a pulsing mid-ring, and a pulsing center dot. The system's one authored ambient animation.
components.html: <svg class="ds-ring-mark" width="36" height="36" viewBox="0 0 36 36" fill="none"><circle cx="18" cy="18" r="15.5" stroke="#2a3542" stroke-width="1"/><circle class="ds-pulse" cx="18" cy="18" r="6" stroke="#4fd3e8" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle class="ds-pulse" cx="18" cy="18" r="1.6" fill="#4fd3e8"/></svg>
components.css: .ds-ring-mark { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 8px rgba(79,211,232,0.4)); } .ds-pulse { animation: ds-pulse 3.2s ease-in-out infinite; transform-origin: 50% 50%; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.55; } 50% { opacity: 1; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-pulse { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview: raygent's brand mark is a steel-blue armored dragon rendered as a sci-fi guardian statue -- glowing cyan tech-rings, dark charcoal ground, faint circuit linework. The dashboard is that guardian's instrument panel: a console you check late at night to see the state of everything it watches over. It does not perform 'dashboard.' It reads as a single sealed plate of dark alloy with one live channel -- cyan -- reserved for the number that matters and the signal that's still moving. Built for a solo founder glancing at this on a laptop at 1am: dark by scene (not by category default), high enough contrast to read fast in a dim room, and structured as one continuous panel rather than a shelf of identical boxes, because a guardian's console has one surface, not a grid of cards pretending to be separate machines. Rejected explicitly: the generic 'dark GitHub card grid' -- same-size bordered tiles, a hero-metric template repeated N times, a random neon accent with no lineage. Every product here is a row on one console, not its own floating card.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, no exceptions: cyan/steel-blue is the entire color vocabulary beyond charcoal and text.
One continuous panel (the console), rows divided by hairlines, never N separately bordered cards.
Tabular monospace for every number; self-hosted Rajdhani for the wordmark and structural labels.
A single authored ambient motion (the ring mark's pulse); everything else is a state, not an effect.
Real data only: DAU is only claimed when events carry an identity.

rules.name: The One Channel Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the only accent in the system. A new element needing emphasis gets more of the existing cyan (size, weight, glow), never a second hue.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Any number compared across rows renders in the monospace data face with tabular-nums, so figures line up.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: Depth is authored once, on the console panel. No row, stat, or label gets its own shadow.

rules.name: The Real Signal Rule
rules.body: The 14-day activity readout only ever encodes real per-day counts, never decoration standing in for data that isn't there.

dos: Do keep revenue the largest, only-glowing figure on every row.
Do add new products as new rows in the existing console, never as a new card or a second console.
Do use the monospace data face for any new numeric readout compared across rows.
Do keep hairlines as the only divider language; no colored border-left/border-right on any element.
Do say 'events today' (never DAU) when events carry no userId/sessionId.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue for anything (status, success, warning).
Don't wrap a product's row in its own border, shadow, or border-radius.
Don't add a second ambient animation.
Don't use a sparkline, progress ring, or bar chart as decoration.
